definition: How close repeated measured values of a quantity are to each other; recording a reading to the right precision means giving every figure the instrument can show.
The reading an instrument gives when the true value is zero; subtract it from every reading (adding it back if it is below zero) to get the true values.
A measurement is repeatable if you get the same or a very similar value when you measure it again in the same way and in the same conditions, during one experiment.
A measurement is reproducible if a similar value is found by another method, in other conditions, or in a separate experiment.
